name: Anguilla
summary: Anguilla has no forced heirship and a will can leave the estate as the owner wishes. Common-law trusts are available and a private foundation can be set up under the Anguilla Foundation Act. The Hague Trusts Convention is not listed as extended to Anguilla.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Anguilla's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
trust_note: Anguilla is not among the UK's territorial extensions on the HCCH page. A 1998 article says the Trusts Ordinance protects against forced heirship claims; a draft Anguilla Special Trust bill (2021) was proposed. Foundations: Anguilla Foundation Act, Cap. A62 (Act 10/2008, in force 12 December 2008, amended 2009 and 2014).
open_questions: Whether Anguilla recognises family provision claims was not found.
Whether the Special Trust (ASTrA) bill was enacted is unknown.
No source read confirms forced heirship is absent; this rests on Anguilla's English-derived common law.
Current Trusts Act name and text not read.
